subject: chemistry
title: Element Encounter: Period 3 with Oxygen and Water
welcome_lead: React Period 3 elements with oxygen, water and chlorine.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Period 3 elemental reactions.
final_note: You met every Period 3 element on the reactivity battlefield.

concepts.def: Slow with cold; vigorous with steam -> MgO.
Most form oxides; vary in vigour.
Unreactive with water at standard T.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Na: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2 (vigorous, fizzes, floats, melts).

Mg: very slow with cold water giving Mg(OH)2 (slightly alkaline). Mg + H2O(g) -> MgO + H2 (with steam, hot).

4Na + O2 -> 2Na2O. 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO (bright white flame). 4Al + 3O2 -> 2Al2O3.

Si + O2 -> SiO2 (slow). P4 + 5O2 -> P4O10 (spontaneous in air). S + O2 -> SO2; further to SO3 with catalyst.

2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl. Mg + Cl2 -> MgCl2. 2Al + 3Cl2 -> 2AlCl3 (covalent, dimerises to Al2Cl6).

Si + 2Cl2 -> SiCl4 (covalent liquid, hydrolyses in water). P4 + 6Cl2 -> 4PCl3 (or PCl5 in excess).

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: Why does atomic radius increase down a group?
options: Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Atoms get bigger down a group because they have more protons attracting more matter.
Each successive element has an additional electron shell, increasing the distance of outer electrons from the nucleus.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
